subject.title: Gateway crash-loops with default Node heap (~4 GB) — make 'openclaw daemon install' set NODE_OPTIONS or accept a --heap-mb flag

question: Should the managed Gateway heap fix land as the fixed 8192 MB service default in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96250, or should maintainers require a tunable heap-size surface before resolving this issue?
rationale: The issue is a valid crash-loop report, but the permanent shape changes daemon startup defaults and resource behavior while touching a security-sensitive env boundary.

options.title: Land the fixed default
options.body: Accept the open PR's fixed heap-only generated service default as the emergency mitigation and track durable tuning separately.

options.title: Require tuning first
options.body: Pause the current fix until a CLI/config/doctor-backed heap-size surface is designed and proven across upgrade paths.

options.title: Diagnostic-only path
options.body: Add status or doctor warnings without changing service startup defaults, leaving operators to opt into their own heap policy.

recommendation.title: Land the fixed default
recommendation.body: Accept the open PR's fixed heap-only generated service default as the emergency mitigation and track durable tuning separately.

likelyOwner.reason: Current history points to this account as the recent carrier of the affected daemon service install surface.
